recipes.name: Different Chicken Divan
ingredients_raw: 2 cups cooked, cubed chicken breast meat
1 pound fresh broccoli, cooked and chopped
1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of chicken soup
1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Spread chicken in the bottom of a 9x13-inch baking dish and scatter broccoli over top.

In a medium bowl, combine mayonnaise, curry powder, cayenne pepper, garlic salt, salt, and pepper, and mix well. Add 1 cup Cheddar cheese, cream of chicken soup, and cream of mushroom soup and mix again, then pour mixture over chicken and broccoli. Sprinkle with remaining 1 1/2 cups of cheese and top with onions.
Bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Different Chicken Divan
raw_recipe.description: The classic chicken divan casserole includes chicken breast, mayonnaise, creamy soup and broccoli; this version adds curry, red pepper and fried onions. It’s the best.

review.reviewBody:
Hi,

I am the author of this recipe. I had a change of last name..lol
Anyway I have lost my original name and can't get it back if I wanted to, I have tried to get them to give me my account back under my new name but so far no luck!
The reason I am writing is to let you guys know that this dish IS supposed to be served over white rice and yes by all means cut down on the curry if you like, I use 1 TBLSP.
I am so happy that most people have enjoyed this recipe! If you like something MUCH milder, try Lisa Adams chicken noodle casserole. Another thing about this recipe that I have started doing over time is not adding the crunchy onions until the last 5 minutes of baking time. I will get around to posting more recipes under my new name soon.
Thx again and Bon Appetit! 08-25-04

Delicious and easy to make! I took the suggestions of the author (thank you!) and other reviewers: did not add any salt, reduced curry, and waited to top with onions until 10 mins remaining in the oven. Most canned soup contains a lot of salt, so no need to add more. I used original Campbell's soups. My family is not a big fan of curry (I am) and 1 Tbsp (curry powder) was a reasonable compromise. 1.5 Tbsp per the recipe would be too much for most people. Of course this all depends on your specific ingredients. The sauce was too thick to pour and stayed on top of the broccoli and chicken. Next time I will add a little water to thin it enough to "pour" and get down into the broc and chicken.

Made some modifications to make a little more healthy. Used 98% fat free cream soups, subbed yogurt for the mayo and doubled the broccoli and only used 1 1/2 cups of cheese. Took previous review suggestion of cooking longer to save on the prep and also added some fresh squeezed lemon juice. Fabulous base recipe that’s easy to modify to your family’s tastes.

My whole family loved it. I used half lite sour cream and half lite mayo, added a can of chicken broth to make a thinner gravy, garlic powder instead of garlic salt, no extra salt, half the curry and cayenne, low sodium soups, half the cheese and mixed everything all together. Ate over rice. So Yummy!

I have made this dish many times and it is a crowd-pleaser! I always like to keep the ingredients on hand so it is easy to assemble them at the last minute. I use the $4.95 rotisserie chicken from Costco, cut up chicken chunks, and freeze it in 3-cup portions. I also use fresh or frozen broccoli in 3-cup portions (cook/defrost before adding). Adding 2 T of lemon juice to the creamy soup mixture adds really good flavor - try it, you will like it! I use sharp cheddar freshly grated for richer flavor. Adding the fried onions for the last 10 minutes is plenty. Serve over steamed rice - YUM!

Yummy and RICH!!!! I added leftover turkey breast with my cooked chicken breast, used 2 cans cream of mushroom soup because I don't like the chicken pieces in cream of chicken soup, used half the amount of cayenne pepper for fear it would be too spicy on my sensitive tummy, didn't add the onions but added a lot more cheese on the top and to the sauce, and used my Braun hand held mixer to blend the sauce. I also baked for an hour. I ate some when this was ready at half hour over rice. There was water under the chicken, and the sauce(to me) didn't seem cooked enough as it hadn't made it's way to the bottom of the baking dish . After an hour the sauce spread to the bottom of the dish and seemed to enhance the savoury flavors of the curry and cayenne. Again this is very good, and very rich!!

This is a very decadent dish, but it is my go-to for church meal train and I have had ladies announce their pregnancy and then promptly ask me to bring them this dish after their baby is born ?? I make it with both carrots and broccoli (I’ve used frozen but prefer fresh just due to texture). My other modifications are to use cream of cheese condensed soup instead of what is listed. I’m not a curry fan, so I’ve never added that. Also, I usually omit or cut wayyyy back on the? cayenne pepper since I’m usually making it for others and am not sure about their spice preferences. I will add a bit of paprika for the red flecks and to give it some Smokey flavor. Also, I like to mix the mayo, spices, and soup in a large bowl and then dump everything else in - reserving some fried onions and cheese to top at the end. Then I put it in a baking dish, bake, and then top with remaining cheese and onions and bake for a few more minutes to melt and get crisp. Seriously the best comfort food ever!!!

I loved this recipe! The only changes I made were: 

Instead of fresh broccoli, I took a bag of frozen chopped broccoli and placed it in the casserole dish frozen, it cooked up just fine. I also used 1/4 cup of sour cream and 3/4 cup of mayo. I also used shredded chicken that I had made via crockpot during the day (just threw some chicken breasts and chicken broth or water in a crockpot and cooked it at low all day). It saved me alot of time by making the chicken that way and using frozen broccoli. I served it over steamed rice. 

One other note, this recipe does have a bite to it. I might scale back on the Curry and Cayenne a little bit next time. But it is still very good.

Excellent. Used square cake pan and used only one can of chicken soup and some sour cream. Added onions for the last 10 minutes. Served with rice.2n time, made for Sunday supper. Added Italian sausage, both soups. Made red rectangle casserole dish and was all gone.

I didn’t have curry, cream of chicken or French fried onions so I made a few changes. I added 5 oz plain Chobani yogurt, and 8 oz tomato sauce and I added 5 cheese tortellini to chicken and added Brussels sprouts with broccoli. I wouldn’t add any salt next time because I thought it was a bit salty, and if I did Brussels again I would cut them into quarters instead of halves. This was pretty heavy, but definitely tasty. I would make it again and modify ingredients again.

I cut the recipe in half, for that reason I use 1 can of Campbell's cream of mushroom and chicken soup since it adds just the right flavor. BE SURE to use curry, maybe not as much as stated, but start with just a little and you'll never want it without it again, it makes the whole dish come together. Instead of dried onions for topping, I've used either crushed potato chips or Ritz crushed with melted butter. You will never find a better recipe, thanks for sharing MRSADAMS - Lisa Brown!!!
Great taste I'm keeping this recipe.
Great recipe! Always well received. I added a generous squirt of lemon juice. Brightened it up! Served over quinoa.

This is the recipe that introduced me to curry many years ago. We absolutely love this meal. I’ll often double the chicken and broccoli instead of eating it over rice and the sauce still has plenty to go around. Must make!
Awesome! Big fan. I left out the cayenne pepper cause my wife didn’t want it Incredible. I read someone here put shrooms in it. I am all over that next time. Thanks again
Loved this recipe! Going to fix it next time though with a healthier creamy curry sauce that leaves the mayo and soups out.
I doubled the chicken and next time I will cut they cayenne pepper in half. Everyone really liked it. Will definitely make again.
Delicious! Added sautéed mushrooms and used green beans instead of broccoli. Also, used cauliflower rice for me. My boys had pasta. Definitely a family favorite!

My family loves this recipe! I also make lunch for a local non-profit once a week and the people there really enjoy this comfort food. It is salty, so I suggest using low-sodium condensed soups and replacing garlic salt with garlic powder. This is an absolute keeper!

I love this recipe and make this dish a lot. A few things I've done to personalize: I've reduced the curry and cayenne to half of what the recipe calls for, I sometimes add cooked carrots to it and I almost always have a layer of stuffing on the bottom as my husband prefers it. I will serve it over rice when I'm the only one eating it.
